Definition
Identifying a faulted component in an RL series circuit may require voltage or resistance measurements.
INTRODUCTIONM
Voltage measurements can quickly determine if the circuit is working correctly.
Resistance measurements can isolate the fault to either the resistor or the inductor.
Knowing which measurement to use will help you easily identify RL series circuit faults.
Let's begin the lesson on RL SERIES CIRCUIT TROUBLESHOOTING EXPERIMENT......
LESSON MENU
RL SERIES CIRCUIT FAULT
The three most common faults in an RL series circuit are open, short and changed value..
DISCUSSION
Let's look at each fault separately to identify the effect on circuit operation and determine how to isolate the fault.
This RL series circuit conducts current according to component values and develops a voltage drop across each component.

A circuit with a changed value resistor or inductor changes circuit values.
Measuring the voltage drops quickly shows there is a problem in the circuit.
However, voltage measurements can not determine which component changed value.
Since Er is less than the calculated value, resistance has decreased in value or inductance has increased in value (XL increases).
Resistance measurements are used to determine which component changed value.

A circuit with an open resistor does not allow current flow.
Measuring the voltage drops quickly shows that there is a problem in the circuit.
However, voltage measurements can not determine if R1 is open or if L1 is shorted.
If R1 is open, current does not flow and the applied voltage is measured across the open resistor.
If L1 is shorted, all the applied voltage is dropped across R1.
Resistance measurements are used to determine if R1 is open or L1 is shorted.
Measure the resistance of R1 by opening S1. Note
To check if L1 is shorted, measure resistance. If 0 ohms, L1 is shorted. Inductors that are not shorted, measure small amounts of resistance.
Remember, an open resistor does not allow current flow and the applied voltage is measured across it.
A circuit with an open inductor does not allow current flow.
Measuring the voltage drops quickly shows there is a problem in the circuit.
However, voltage measurements can not determine if L1 is open or R1 is shorted.
If L1 is open, current does not flow and the applied voltage is measured across the open inductor.
If R1 is shorted, all the applied voltage is dropped across L1.
Resistance measurements are used to determine if L1 is open or R1 is shorted.
Measure the resistance of R1 by opening S1. Note
To check if L1 is open, measure resistance. If infinity, L1 is open. Inductors that are not open, measure small amounts of resistance.
The meter indicates that R1 is good. The fault is an open inductor.
Remember, an open inductor does not allow current flow and the applied voltage is measured across it.

Measuring the voltage drops quickly shows there is a problem in the circuit.

If R1 is shorted, all the applied voltage is dropped across L1.
If L1 is open, current does not flow and the applied voltage is measured across the open inductor.
Resistance measurements are used to determine if R1 is shorted or L1 is open.
Measure the resistance of R1 by opening S1. Note

Remember, a shorted resistor does not have a voltage drop and the applied voltage is measured across the inductor.
A circuit with a shorted inductor eliminates the effect of inductance in the circuit.
Measuring the voltage drops quickly shows there is a problem in the circuit.
However, voltage measurements can not determine if L1 is shorted or R1 is open.
If L1 is shorted, all of the applied voltage is dropped across R1.
If R1 is open, current does not flow and the applied voltage is measured across the open resistor.
